item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was a big weekend for New York Rangers prospects playing in the NCAA. A rematch of last season’s Frozen Four semifinal highlighted the schedule, while three Rangers prospects combined for five goals. The new USA Hockey Men’s College Hockey Poll on Monday brought more good news for the organization’s NCAA prospects. Michigan’s sweep of Denve r, combined with Western Michigan’s sweep of Notre Dame, resulted in Rangers prospects occupying spots on each of the nation’s top five ranked teams: Michigan (Malcom Spence) Michigan State (Sean Barnhill) North Dakota (E.J. Emery) Western Michigan (Ty Henricks) Denver (Ben MacBeath) Each of the top five teams features a Rangers prospect, and all five are considered early contenders for the national championship. A sixth Rangers prospect, Charlie Morrison, also remains in the top-20 rankings as his UConn Huskies moved up to No. 16 this week. That gives the Rangers six ranked teams among their seven NCAA prospects. First Star: Malcom Spence, Michigan Few — if any — games on the early-season college hockey schedule generated as much attention as the showdown Friday between No. 1 Denver and No. 2 Michigan. The matchup was a rematch of last season’s Frozen Four semifinal, won by Denver on its way to another national championship victory. This time it was Michigan earning some revenge. The Wolverines skated away with a 4-1 victory, snapping Denver’s 19-game winning streak dating back to last season. Leading the way was Malcolm Spence, the Rangers key forward prospect who scored twice, including the game-winning goal. With Michigan already leading 1-0 in the second period, a Denver turnover created an odd-man rush. Spence finished off a give-and-go sequence to double Michigan’s advantage. The two teams met again Saturday, with Michigan completing the weekend sweep via a 4-3 victory. Spence was held off the score sheet in this one, and picked up a roughing minor penalty. Spence is third on the Wolverines with four goals in six games, and his seven points are tied for fifth. In addition, his 14 penalty minutes rank second on Michigan, and he’s scored on a whopping 50 percent of his shots, so far (4 for 8). Emery has two points (one goal, one assist) in four games, and leads North Dakota with a plus-5 rating. Charlie Morrison, UConn Charlie Morrison continued to gain experience in the 16th-ranked UConn lineup, when the Huskies split a weekend series with 13th-ranked Colorado College. The Huskies eventually claimed a 3-2 overtime victory over the Tigers. The assist was the second of Morrison’s NCAA career. He finished with two shots on goal and a plus-2 rating. Morrison was held without a shot on goal and finished the game at minus-1 as the Tigers controlled play for much of the night. Barnhill earned his point on his team’s fourth goal of the game in the third period. For Barnhill, it is his first point of the season and fifth career point (no goals) in 40 NCAA games. Raoul Boilard, Lake Superior State Raoul Boilard and Lake Superior State made the long trip to Alaska for a two-game series against Alaska Anchorage and came away with a split. Friday’s opener got off to a rough start for the Lakers, who found themselves trailing 3-0 after the opening period. Boilard helped spark an attempted comeback in the second period. With Lake Superior State still searching for momentum, Boilard fired a shot on goal that produced a rebound. Markus Loponen collected the loose puck and scored to cut the deficit to 3-1. The play gave Boilard his third assist of the season. He finished the night with four shots on goal, an assist, a 9-for-20 performance in the face-off circle and a minus-1 rating. Despite narrowing the gap, the Lakers eventually fell 5-2. Saturday brought a better result for Lake Superior State, which earned a 4-2 victory to salvage a split of the series. Boilard did not register a point and was held without a shot on goal, but finished 8-for-13 on fac-eo

item.title: Lord Botham 'proud' of leukaemia fundraising walks
item.description: Lord Ian Botham played cricket for England from 1977 to 1992 [Getty Images] Former England cricketer Lord Ian Botham says he is "proud" of his fundraising walks for leukaemia research, describing them as "a lot of fun and pain". The former Somerset player raised more than £12m for charity, with his first walk taking place in 1985. Lord Botham said the challenges started after he saw four children at Musgrove Park Hospital in Taunton when he was receiving treatment for a broken foot. "The doctor said well you've got eight to ten weeks for treatment and I don't think those boys will be with us and, at the end of my treatment, they weren't. I said to Kath, we have to do something positive." He added: "It's all about awareness. The leukaemia walks was the awareness and in those days there was a 20% chance of survival, now it's a 94 to 95% chance. So that is terrific." The money raised by Lord Botham over the last four decades has supported Blood Cancer UK (formerly Leukaemia Research). Lord Botham completed several charity fundraising walks with the first in 1985 [BBC Archive] He talked about the impact of his walks while discussing his new book, Seasons: Riding the Torpedo, during an interview with BBC Breakfast. "We did 18 walks, ten and a half thousand miles, that is the equivalent from London to Sydney. "It started off we didn't know what we were going to achieve, we didn't know it was going to work out, but the response from the public was immense." He completed his final UK trek in 1999, with the last fundraising walk in 2013. More from Somerset Farmer feels 'helpless' after bluetongue outbreak 'Shoplifting is getting worse - but police won't help' Guide dog puppies taken on cave training trip The all-rounder, who represented England from 1976 to 1992, said a lot of "sacrifices" were made to make the walks and his cricket career possible. "It was a family affair," he continued. "The toughest job of the lot and that's the organisation. These walks took about 18 months to organise with my wife and children." "I get a lot of stick from the grandchildren, they said to me, you were the worst father because I was never there. I was all over the world playing cricket. "When the grandchildren came along, I got a big mug one morning saying best ever granddad. So it balanced out, but yeah, you do make a lot of sacrifices. That's where the family comes together." item.title: Is Stephen Curry playing tonight? Warriors vs. Lakers injury report to open season
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Is Stephen Curry playing tonight? Warriors vs. Lakers injury report to open season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors will be facing the Los Angeles Lakers to open their season, and the main question surrounding the team is: Will Stephen Curry play? During an open practice, Curry suffered a non-contact injury , and though he wanted to give the fans a sign that he was okay, he ended up walking back to the locker room. The fans held their breath, but after practice, head coach Steve Kerr noted that he was fine. The next day, Curry was a full participant at practice , and Kerr said that he would be good to go against the Lakers. At the same time, he’s still listed on the injury report, and it won’t be official until he takes the floor. Here is Curry’s injury status heading into the season opener. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Stephe n Curry’s injury status vs. Lakers Curry is listed as probable against the Lakers, which means it’s highly likely he plays. That’s good news for the Warriors, as they don’t want to be without their ace already. This team will go as far as Curry takes them, and he gives them the best chance to win whenever he’s on the court. The Warriors are already dealing with a few injuries to their key players. Of course, Jimmy Butler is still rehabbing from his ACL injury last year, and there’s no telling when he’ll be back on the court. Kristaps Porzingis is still dealing with the illness that he’s had for the last few years. The Warriors don’t know when he’ll return, and Porzingis doesn’t know either. The most recent player is Brandin Podziemski, who has been ruled out with low back soreness. That means the Warriors will have to roll with what they have, and Curry will be looked upon to lead the group. item.title: Is Ja Morant actually going to come off the bench for Blazers with Damian Lillard returning?
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Is Ja Morant actually going to come off the bench for Blazers with Damian Lillard returning? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Portland Trail Blazers will host the Phoenix Suns at Moda Center on Wednesday for their season opener. All eyes will be on the team’s backcourt, with Damian Lillard returning from an Achilles injury and Ja Morant making his debut. item.description: The Stroker family, four athletes, one coach and a pair of contributors will be inducted at the Ridgewood High School Athletics Hall of Game banquet Oct. 24 at the Brick House in Wyckoff. Ceremonies begin with a social hour at 6 p.m. with a sit-down dinner to follow. The Stroker Family The Stroker Family has contributed to the Ridgewood High School community for almost 100 years. Jack E. Stroker was a soccer and basketball player in the 1930s who married standout swimmer Virginia, who was a Ridgewood High School cheerleader. Jack B. Stroker (Class of 1965) and Jim Stroker (Class of 1970) were the next generation. Jack B. worked for the Ridgewood Board of Education and was also a youth coach. Jim became a legendary coach in multiple sports for the Maroons. George Rork The Hall of Fame class also includes George Rork (Class of 1968), a standout tennis player who was part of two Group 4 state championship teams before playing at U. Penn. Blair Fuentez Blair Fuentez (Class of 2011) was an All-County selection in volleyball for the Maroons and still holds the school record for kills with 905. She played for four years as a setter at Miami. Mark Kossick Mark Kossick (Class of 1993) played four different sports at Ridgewood, excelling at them all and was hailed by former football coach Chuck Johnson as the most complete player to ever wear maroon. He remains the all-time leading scorer in football and was a first-team All-County pick in swimming and tennis. Stuart Mozeleski Inducted posthumously, Stuart Mozeleski (Class of 1958) was a stellar football player and golfer. “Stu” led the Maroons to undefeated football seasons in 1956 and 1957 and a pair of North Bergen Interscholastic League titles. He was captain of the Maroons golf team in 1958. Nancy Hyman Coach Nancy Hyman became the Maroons' head boys tennis coach in 1989 and led them to a pair of Group 4 State titles, 11 sectional titles and 11 league championships. When she retired in 2002, she had a career record of 303-33. Dan D’Uva and Guy Benson The broadcasting duo of Dan D’Uva and Guy Benson changed the way Ridgewood High School athletics were delivered, creating the popular RHS Sports on-campus network. Both men parlayed their broadcasting days at Ridgewood into professional success. item.title: Why NFL has 'no concern' about Joe Buck, Troy Aikman ESPN contract drama
item.description: The NFL is not concerned with the bubbling drama between ESPN "Monday Night Football" announcers Joe Buck and Troy Aikman. Aikman and Buck got into a disagreement prior to the Oct. 12 "MNF" game between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams regarding Buck's recent contract extension with ESPN, according to Front Office Sports. Aikman remains unsigned beyond the Super Bowl on Feb. 14, 2027, which is ESPN's first-ever Super Bowl and the first on ABC in 20 years. Aikman essentially confirmed the argument during an interview on a local Dallas radio station last week and said he looks forward to being a broadcasting free agent after the season . Buck and Aikman did not address the situation publicly before they called the Washington Commanders and San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 19. "No concern," NFL executive vice president for media distribution and chief media officer Hans Schroeder said Wednesday at the NFL's fall owners' meeting. "I don’t know if you watched the game on Monday night, it was an incredible game, and incredible coverage by Joe and Troy, just like they always do." Schroeder noted the other ways Disney, which owns ESPN, covered the game. Pat McAfee’s alt-cast debuted (for an NFL game), for example. This will be the first Super Bowl that Buck and Aikman have called together since Super Bowl 54, which was the Kansas City Chiefs' first of three recent championships, in February 2020. They called six Super Bowls together at FOX and left the network for ESPN together before the 2022 season. "Look, that’s something that we’re really not involved with," Schroeder said of monitoring broadcast partners' announcing teams. "I think the fans are deserving of first-class game production, which Joe and Troy have (done) going back to (2002) … a history of doing as well as anyone. And I think we’ll continue to see them do that as well as anyone. "We’re incredibly excited about the year ahead and the Super Bowl and their coverage and getting them back." item.title: Monaco manager Filipe Luís refutes ‘favourites’ tag in Europa Conference League
item.description: Monaco manager Filipe Luís refutes ‘favourites’ tag in Europa Conference League AS Monaco didn’t necessarily want to qualify for the UEFA Europa Conference League, but having done so, they have inherited a position as one of the favourites to win the competition. Les Monégasques competed in the UEFA Champions League last season and had the objective of qualifying for that same competition last season. They fell short. It is the first time that the Principality club are competing in the UECL and there is a certain pressure to go far in the competition. Alongside Brighton and Hove Albion and Freiburg, who lost to Aston Villa in last season’s UEFA Europa League final, they are considered one of the favourites. Speaking in a press conference attended by Get French Football News, Filipe Luís played it down. “Favourites? I don’t think so. As Hansi Flick (Barcelona manager) said on Tuesday, you only win titles in May and June. It is impossible to do so now,” said the Monaco manager. He added, “We have a lot of things to prove […] it is only at the end of the season that we will see our team’s true level.” GFFN | Luke Entwistle – reporting from Monaco

item.title: Lahm calls for consequences for FIFA's Infantino and Manchester City
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Former Germany captain Philipp Lahm speaks at a press conference ahead of the induction ceremony for the "German Sports Hall of Fame." (is associated with: «Lahm calls for consequences for FIFA's Infantino and Manchester City») Boris Roessler/dpa Former Germany captain Philipp Lahm has welcomed the criticism on FIFA president Gianni Infantino and the investigation against Manchester City over financial irregularities. "If behaviour such as that seen in Manchester and at FIFA is punished, that is a good thing," the 2014 World Cup winner Lahm wrote in a column for Die Zeit weekly. "Football must prevent questionable ideas from distancing it even further from its grassroots. Only then can it foster engagement with civil society; only then can it help to strengthen Europe." City were found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules between 2009 and 2018 by an independent commission, a verdict they are appealing. They could reportedly face a significant points deduction which would lead to Premier League relegation. "It is good when the Premier League takes firm action against unfair competition," Lahm said. Infantino has come under fire on several fronts: such as the eventually abandoned plan to bring private investors into their events led by the World Cup, the awarding of a FIFA peace price to US President Donald Trump and the affair around US player Folarin Balogun who was allowed to play a World Cup game despite being sent off in the previous match after a phone call from Trump to Infantino. UEFA has sent FIFA 42 questions it wants to be answered on those issues. It wants Infantino to resign but Infantino has said he will seek re-election in March. "I also welcome the fact that rules apply in other cases. UEFA is taking a hard line with Gianni Infantino," Lahm said, adding: "The FIFA president may be brought down."

item.title: Benson and McNabney handed first Ireland call-ups
item.description: Jamie Benson, who can play at fly-half or centre, joined Ulster from Harlequins in the summer [Getty Images] Ulster duo Jamie Benson and James McNabney have been handed their first Ireland call-ups for November's Nations Championship matches. Former England Under-20 international Benson joined Ulster from Harlequins in the off-season and is Irish qualified through his Belfast-born mother. The 24-year-old has featured at centre for the majority of his short Ulster career to date but can also play at fly-half. Back row McNabney, 23, had been in Ireland training squads before and returned to action over the summer after a year on the sidelines with an ACL injury. Prop Andrew Porter, forward Ryan Baird and wings Mack Hansen and Tommy O'Brien all return to the squad after missing the summer's matches. Head coach Andy Farrell has a had to deal with a lengthy injury list, with captain Caelan Doris among those sidelined. Fly-half Jack Crowley is also missing through injury, as is Jack Boyle, Harry Byrne, Jack Conan, Iain Henderson, Paddy McCarthy, Calvin Nash and Bryn Ward. In the absence of Doris, his Leinster team-mate Dan Sheehan will captain Ireland. Despite not featuring for Leinster this season, scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park has been named. The Ulster duo of Zac Ward and Cormac Izuchukwu have missed out on selection, as has Munster prop Jeremy Loughman. Ireland will face Argentina at the Aviva Stadium on Friday, 6 November before Fiji travel to Dublin on 14 November. Farrell's side then host world champions South Africa on 21 November before the finals weekend at the Allianz Stadium in London the following week. Ireland started their Nations Championship campaign with victories over Australia and Japan but New Zealand came out on top in the third summer Test. Ireland squad Forwards: Ryan Baird, Tadhg Beirne, Billy Bohan, Thomas Clarkson, Tadhg Furlong, Sam Illo, Sean Jansen, Ronan Kelleher, Joe McCarthy, James McNabney, Darragh Murray, Tom O'Toole, Andrew Porter, Cian Prendergast, James Ryan, Dan Sheehan (captain), Tom Stewart, Nick Timoney, Josh van der Flier. Backs: Bundee Aki, Rob Baloucoune, Jamie Benson, Craig Casey, Nathan Doak, Ciaran Frawley, Jamison Gibson-Park, Mack Hansen, Robbie Henshaw, Hugo Keenan, Stuart McCloskey, Jimmy O'Brien, Tommy O'Brien, Jamie Osborne, Sam Prendergast, Garry Ringrose, Jacob Stockdale.

The San Diego Padres fell short in the postseason and need reinforcments for next year. Mostly, San Diego's front office will be targeting the free-agent starting pitching and trade market. Michael King can opt out of the final two years of his contract, and midseason trade acquisitions Casey Mize and Robbie Ray are soon to become free agents. Nick Pivetta can also test free agency if he so chooses. "The Padres' rotation is now headlined by Joe Musgrove, who has not pitched in a regular season game since 2024, and Randy Vasquez, who is a back-end starter at best. Last month, ESPN pundit Dan Orlovsky said Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (compared to Hurts) is “what it should look like.” What about Hurts doesn’t look like how a quarterback is supposed to look? I thought a quarterback should look like a Super Bowl MVP? A better question is: how would any ex-backup quarterback, paid to define what a good, great, or elite quarterback looks like, know what that quarterback actually looks like? I assume because they’re familiar with what it doesn’t look like, but I digress. Start your day with essential news from Salon. Sign up for our free morning newsletter , Crash Course. item.description: India begin a 12-match tour of New Zealand on October 22, and the trip is one of the longest and most demanding assignments on their 2026 calendar. The two sides meet in five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests, with play spread across six venues and running all the way through to December 1. Shreyas Iyer leads the side in the T20I leg, while Shubman Gill takes charge of the ODI and Test squads. MAKE YOUR BET WITH DAFABET AND GET UP TO 200% WELCOME BONUS The Test series carries World Test Championship points, and India will be looking to end a long wait for a series win in New Zealand, having not managed one since 2009. Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source Time difference between IST and NZST New Zealand operates on New Zealand Standard Time (NZST), which is UTC+12 and sits six and a half hours ahead of Indian Standard Time. However, that is not the clock the country is running on during this tour. Between late September and early April, New Zealand switches to New Zealand Daylight Time (NZDT), which is UTC+13. Every match on this tour falls inside that window, so the gap between the two countries is seven and a half hours. In practical terms, when it is 8:00 p.m. in Christchurch, it is 12:30 p.m. in Mumbai on the same day. New Zealand has a single time zone across all six venues on this tour, so the conversion stays the same whether the match is in Auckland, Wellington, Hamilton, Tauranga or Christchurch. What time are India vs New Zealand matches? The three formats all start at different times, and the difference is significant for Indian viewers. The T20Is are the most convenient, beginning at 12:30 p.m. IST, as they are evening fixtures in New Zealand. The ODIs start at 7:30 a.m. IST, while the Tests get under way at 3:30 a.m. IST, which means an early alarm for anyone wanting the first session. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is something really rotten about how the Colorado Avalanche have lost their last two games. It’s not that they dropped both. This isn’t the Avalanche we know, and it’s likely not the Avalanche we’ll see for the rest of the season. But right now, as head coach Jared Bednar put it, they’re going to need to do some soul-searching. My thoughts on a poor two-game road trip. Just a couple of weeks ago, I was writing about how the second period had become an issue for Colorado. That came after the Avs gave up three goals on four shots to the Toronto Maple Leafs in the middle frame and surrendered three goals to the Los Angeles Kings in that same period. Now, it’s the first period that’s hurting them. The slow starts have become a problem. Colorado gave up two goals to the Pittsburgh Penguins before getting going in that game. Against the Philadelphia Flyers and New Jersey Devils, they’ve surrendered the first goal both times and been outshot by a combined 28-12 in the opening periods. 2. It took until Jan. 4-6 last season for Nathan MacKinnon to go consecutive games without recording a point. He failed to get on the scoresheet in either of Colorado’s last two games. 3. I’ve seen debates over the years about whether faceoff success rates matter as much as we think they do, and I’m willing to hear those arguments out. But when the gap is this big, and you’re winning just 35% of your draws, it’s a problem. It’s part of why you’re spending so much time chasing the game. 4. Nazem Kadri is going to bury one of these chances at some point, right? He’s as snakebitten as they come, even as Bednar continues to trot him out there for 20+ minutes per night. He’s done enough to deserve that ice time, at least in my opinion, but my goodness, he needs to get one in the back of the net to end this drought. 5. This was a pretty shocking stat to see, courtesy of my colleague Corey Masisak of the Denver Post . Before Tuesday in New Jersey, the Avalanche hadn’t allowed 40+ shots on goal in a game since Dec. 12. Before that, they’d done it only one other time since the start of the 2024-25 season. They’re essentially averaging one game per season in which they give up 40+ shots. Insane. 6. item.description: Martin O’Neill’s Celtic change of heart explained after managerial doubts Former Celtic manager Gordon Strachan believes Martin O’Neill has rediscovered his enthusiasm for the job after considering his future at Parkhead earlier this month. item.description: headlinephotos/Depositphotos headlinephotos/Depositphotos LeBron James explains helicopter travel LeBron Raymone James Sr., a professional basketball player for the Philadelphia 76ers, addressed questions about his helicopter commute between New York City and Philadelphia on October 16, 2026. His travel arrangements have attracted attention ahead of the NBA season. The 41-year-old forward discussed the arrangement after Philadelphia’s preseason finale against the Boston Celtics. James described helicopter travel as another transportation option and confirmed that he had previously used helicopters. headlinephotos/Depositphotos LeBron James responds to criticism LeBron James dismissed concerns about his helicopter commute during a brief exchange with reporters following Philadelphia’s preseason game against Boston. The four-time NBA champion indicated that he considered the arrangement normal transportation. When asked about traveling by helicopter, James responded, “I’ve done it before.” He added that it was simply another way of transportation, offering little further explanation despite growing public interest in his unusual commute. headlinephotos/Depositphotos LeBron James saves time with flights LeBron James uses helicopter transportation to reduce the time spent traveling between New York City and the Philadelphia area. The journey normally takes approximately 90 minutes to two hours by car, depending on traffic conditions. According to Front Office Sports, a helicopter can complete the same trip in approximately 30 minutes. The arrangement allows James to travel between his New York residence and Philadelphia’s basketball facilities without relying on highway traffic. Image Press Agency/Depositphotos LeBron James receives Fanatics flights LeBron James has access to helicopter transportation through his existing endorsement agreement with Fanatics. The sports merchandise company provides corporate aviation services as part of its broader business relationship with the NBA superstar. Front Office Sports reported on October 5 that James does not personally pay for these helicopter trips. His representative confirmed that access to corporate aircraft was included in the partnership established nearly three years earlier. Depositphotos LeBron James signed Fanatics deal in 2024 LeBron James established a multiyear trading card partnership with Fanatics in January 2024 while playing for the Los Angeles Lakers. The agreement includes corporate aviation benefits that became particularly useful following his move to Philadelphia. A spokesperson for James explained that similar transportation arrangements are available to other major athletes working with Fanatics. The company confirmed that the agreement supports James as he divides his time between two cities. item.title: ‘No Olise, no party’ — Is Bayern Munich too reliant on Michael Olise?
item.description: (Photo by Tom Weller/picture alliance via Getty Images) Noted pundit Didi Hamann says Bayern Munich might be a little too dependent on Michael Olise, but do not expect Serge Gnabry to lose sleep over the statement. “No Olise, no party,” Hamann told Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), warning that Bayern’s dependence on the Frenchman is becoming increasingly concerning. “If he doesn’t deliver, nobody else does.” Gnabry was asked about the comments ahead of Bayern Munich’s Champions League clash with Arsenal, and he was not exactly interested in giving Hamann’s take any extra oxygen. Olise, of course, is susp ended for the showdown. “I don’t think a statement like that is going to unsettle us or give us any extra motivation. If something like that appears in the newspapers, we don’t really care. We’re just trying to win games,” Gnabry said. “Michael is one of the outstanding players in our team, delivering incredible performances. We can’t deny that when he doesn’t play, we’re missing a key element of his game. Nevertheless, the team is always prepared to make changes, and we have incredible quality up front, regardless of who plays. That’s why we simply have to give it our all [against Arsenal].” Olise has been phenomenal, but Hamann’s take raises a legitimate question — has Bayern bec ome too dependent on one player to make things happen? Against Arsenal, Bayern Munich will have a chance to show whether the answer is yes — or whether t he rest of the attack can step up when Olise is out. Join the conversation! item.description: Dylan Larkin wants out of Detroit. And the Devils are now among the teams he would be willing to call home. Whether general manager Sunny Mehta wants to — or can — make that happen is another question. The Detroit Free Press reported that Larkin has expanded his list of acceptable trade destinations to 10 teams: the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. Larkin got a taste of it in February, winning an Olympic gold medal with Team USA in Milan, Italy. Now, the 30-year-old center is looking for an opportunity to pursue a Stanley Cup after spending his entire NHL career with the Red Wings, who selected him in the first round of the 2014 draft. Larkin has amassed 277 goals and 648 points in 815 career games. Larkin’s trade request became public over the summer, beginning a saga that has followed Detroit into the regular season. Since then, Larkin has been stripped of the captaincy , heard boos from Red Wings fans and had his image disappear from a captains mural at Little Caesars Arena. While Larkin’s future remains unsettled, he has played with Detroit this year. Larkin has a goal and four assists in seven games. Larkin has scored at least 30 goals in each of the last five seasons. Adding that kind of production to a forward group already featuring Jack Hughes, Nico Hischier, Jesper Bratt and Timo Meier would give the Devils another high-end option up front. It would also give coach Sheldon Keefe more flexibility in how he deploys his forwards. Tonight’s slate of NBA action features 11 matchups, and there’s a ton of fan bases who are excited to see what their squads have to offer. This offseason saw a ton of player movement, with impact players finding new homes. Here are three star players making their regular-season debut with a new NBA franchise. Expectations are high for the Heat, and it will be interesting to see how the 31-year-old does in Miami’s system. That’s all in the past now, and Toronto Raptors fans couldn’t be happier as Leonard returns to The 6ix. Upsets. Coaches glaring, coaches cheering. NIL didn’t matter. Who’s going to make the playdowns didn’t matter. It was the games that mattered. What a day. Maybe the best ever. Lots of upsets. As for predictions last week, not bad. My pick the Fighting Irish got hosed in Provo. But, ya know what, it’s not called South Bend Syndrome for nothing. What goes around comes around, it is said. Alright, yes, I just made up the term South Bend Syndrome. And Oklahoma, where the wind comes sweepin’ down the plain, fell back to their Veneblesier norm. (More about their conquerers below.) Other than that, four bullseyes. Beavers, the other Cougars, Buckeyes and Cardinals. Four up. Two down. 33-21 for this increasingly wackorama season. CoachSpeak of the Week: After his kicker told the coach he made him nervous watching him practice kicks, Alabama’s Gene Stallings advised, “Well, son, I plan on being at all the games.” This Week’s Winners: Texas Tech @ Cincinnati. They are not the Best Team Money Can Buy, the Cody Campbells. But they are undefeated, with dubs over Houston and surprising Oregon State. Coach Satt’s Bearcats started strong, but have dropped two in a row. Both on the road. Their third in a row is in Nippert. Red Raiders. Iowa @ Minnesota. This one’s for the Floyd of Rosedale. A hundred pound pig trophy. The origin of which has something to do with a conflagration in the mid 30s. One state’s governor threatened to beat up the other. Who tried to calm things down by offering a real living porcine being to his threatener if his team lost. Said Floyd of Rosedale. Or something like that. So sure some diehard midwestern fanatic will correct me, while advising that I do fuller research. Maybe Floyd the Barber can make sense of it. To say, this is olden days football rivalry par excellence. The visiting 6-1 (2-1) Hawkeyes are pretty good. The Gophers aren’t bad, though not so Golden last week, when getting throttled at Purdue. PJ Fleck loves the smear of blood after the final whistle. Upset alert. He gets it. Southern California @ Wisconsin. One-two one-two-three uh!/ Hot Pants – hey hot pants uh! Smoking/ Hot pants – smoking that-hot pants/ That’s where its at a-that’s where its at. In non-James Brownian vernacular, the visiting coach in this one’s pants are hot from his hot seat. Despite a 6-1 record, Lincoln Riley’s getting the stink eye from many Trojan faithful. Same was true of Badgers coach Luke Fickell, except to a polka beat. But they’re calmer and somewhat more reasonable in Cheesylvania. And they’re playing better, the residents of Camp Randall. They keep it up. Wisconsin. Vanderbilt @ Kentucky. A hundred pound pig trophy. The origin of which has something to do with a conflagration in the mid 30s. One state’s governor threatened to beat up the other. Who tried to calm things down by offering a real living porcine being to his threatener if his team lost. Said Floyd of Rosedale. Or something like that. So sure some diehard midwestern fanatic will correct me, while advising that I do fuller research. Maybe Floyd the Barber can make sense of it. To say, this is olden days football rivalry par excellence. The visiting 6-1 (2-1) Hawkeyes are pretty good. The Gophers aren’t bad, though not so Golden last week, when getting throttled at Purdue. PJ Fleck loves the smear of blood after the final whistle. Upset alert. He gets it. Southern California @ Wisconsin. One-two one-two-three uh!/ Hot Pants – hey hot pants uh! Smoking/ Hot pants – smoking that-hot pants/ That’s where its at a-that’s where its at. In non-James Brownian vernacular, the visiting coach in this one’s pants are hot from his hot seat. item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
